overall_structure.value: Initial (as-forged billet) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel used as the pre-deformation reference state: large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries, with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations (segregation banding) whose direction changes from grain to grain, indicating chemical heterogeneity.

source.reason: b0018 states the corresponding initial microstructure is shown in Fig. 1, and figure_001 describes large polygonal grains with segregation striations; this is the starting state for the hot-compression sample.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (950 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1) the true stress–true strain flow curve is given in Fig. 3(a); it rises to a peak and then softens to a plateau (peak strain ~0.1–0.2), but no numeric peak/steady-state stress value is tabulated for this specific condition.
This sample lies within the recommended hot-working window for fine and uniform DRX grains, reported as 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086).
The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel (averaged over the experimental range) is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (b0012, b0032, b0085).

The lnZ value for this sample (0.01 s^-1, 950 °C) is 61.27; within the experimental matrix lnZ decreases with increasing T and increases with increasing ε̇, tracking the flow-stress trend (table_001, b0037).

General DRX behavior of the steel: with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T the Z parameter decreases and DRX is more likely to occur, but the DRX grain size increases accordingly; the DRX average grain size after 60% compression increases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0012, b0063).

DRX degree within a compression sample is greatest in the large-deformation zone (region 3), then the small-deformation zone (region 2), and least in the difficult-deformation zone (region 1) (b0060, b0063, figure_008).
